kyushu-university-english-undergraduate-.about:
Kyushu University in Fukuoka, one of Japan's former imperial universities, runs four-year bachelor's programmes taught fully in English: the International Undergraduate Program in the School of Engineering, the Bioresource and Bioenvironment programme (Agriculture) and the School of Interdisciplinary Science and Innovation. Entry is in October.

From the October 2027 applicant pool, Kyushu picks a few candidates with outstanding screening results and recommends them to Japan's Ministry of Education (MEXT). Recipients get exemption from the entrance and tuition fees for four years, a monthly allowance of ¥117,000 and return airfare. The online application system is open only from 7 to 11 December 2026, after which all documents must be posted; some programmes require minimum standardized test scores (SAT, ACT, IB or A-level).
highlights: Full tuition + ¥117,000/month via MEXT
Fully English-taught degrees, October entry
Online window only 7–11 December 2026
kyushu-university-english-undergraduate-.eligibility: International applicants (non-Japanese nationality) to Kyushu's English-taught undergraduate programmes with strong grades and accepted standardized test scores. Open to all nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar; students already holding other aid need a student visa.
how_to_apply: Read the October 2027 application guidelines for your programme
Register on the online system between 7 and 11 December 2026
Post the required documents (transcripts, test scores, recommendations)
Tick scholarship consideration; Kyushu contacts recommended candidates individually
Complete interview/screening and MEXT paperwork if selected
kyushu-university-english-undergraduate-.costs: MEXT recipients: entrance and tuition fees waived for four years, ¥117,000 monthly stipend, return airfare. Non-recipients pay regular national-university fees (about ¥535,800/year).

lafayette-college-financial-aid-internat.about:
Lafayette College in Easton, Pennsylvania, combines liberal arts with engineering. International students can receive institutional need-based grants by submitting the CSS Profile (the ISFAA is not accepted), and Lafayette also awards merit scholarships, for which the CSS Profile is not required.

Admitted students who submit everything on time receive their College Financing Plan online with the admission decision. Deadlines are 15 November for Early Decision I and 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision. Aid must be renewed each year.
highlights: Need-based grants for internationals
Merit scholarships too
Deadline 15 Jan 2027 (RD)
lafayette-college-financial-aid-internat.eligibility: International first-year applicants to Lafayette for fall 2027. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to Lafayette via Common App by 15 Nov (ED I) or 15 Jan (ED II/RD)
Submit the CSS Profile for need-based aid by the same deadline
Check the scholarships page for merit awards
Reapply for aid each year

lakehead-international-entrance-scholars.about:
Lakehead University (Thunder Bay and Orillia, Ontario) awards International Undergraduate Entrance Scholarships automatically for 2027–2028: CA$40,000 (CA$10,000 × 4) for a 90%+ Canadian-equivalent average or IB 35+, CA$30,000 (CA$7,500 × 4) for 80–89.9% or IB 30–34, and a one-time CA$6,000 for 75–79.9%.

The award is stated in your letter of acceptance and is renewable with the same average each year. It applies to non-Canadian citizens entering from high school or transferring from an international institution into a degree of at least four years.

Automatic, listed in the acceptance letter
IB-friendly thresholds (35+ for top tier)

lascala-erasmus-mundus-2027.about:
LASCALA is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) in Large Scale Accelerators and Lasers. A physics and engineering master's on the large particle accelerators and high-power lasers used in research, medicine and industry. It is coordinated by Université Paris-Saclay in Orsay (France); the consortium: Université Paris-Saclay (France), Sapienza University of Rome (Italy), University of Salamanca (Spain) and Lund University (Sweden). Students move between partner universities and graduate with a joint or multiple degree.

tcu-scholarships-need-based-aid-internat.about:
Texas Christian University in Fort Worth gives international first-year students academic scholarships based on achievement and need-based financial aid. Need-based awards range from $2,000 to $41,570 a year; combined packages average about $25,000 and can reach $51,570. Awards are competitive and usually cover less than half the cost of attendance, so families must show substantial resources for the visa.

Apply for admission (academic scholarships are considered with the application; TCU encourages applying by 1 November for top awards) and submit the CSS Profile (code 6820) by 1 February for need-based aid.
